desc:
A string s consists only of the characters '(' and ')'. A bracket string is balanced when every '(' can be paired with a later ')' and every ')' with an earlier '(', with each bracket used in exactly one pair.

You may insert new brackets at any positions. Return the minimum number of insertions needed to make s balanced.
hints: Scan from left to right and keep track of the brackets that are still waiting for a partner.
A ')' that finds no waiting '(' can never be fixed by anything on its left, so it needs one inserted '(' right away.
Keep a counter of unmatched '(' and a counter of insertions. The answer is the insertions plus whatever unmatched '(' are left at the end.
editorial: Treat the string like a stack that only ever holds '(', so a single counter open is enough. For each '(' increase open. For each ')', if open > 0 it cancels one waiting bracket, otherwise it has no partner and we must insert a '(' (count one insertion).

After the scan every remaining waiting '(' needs one inserted ')', so the answer is insertions + open. Each insertion fixes exactly one unmatched bracket and the greedy decisions are forced, so the count is minimal. Time is O(n) with O(1) extra space.
